cultura.name: La Bomba
cultura.description:
An Afro-Puerto Rican music and dance tradition in which dancers interact with the rhythm played by drummers.
It grew from the experiences and creativity of African-descended communities on the island.
cultura.credit: Add verified photographer and image-source credit

cultura.name: La Plena
cultura.description:
A popular musical tradition sometimes described as a sung newspaper because its lyrics can tell stories about everyday events.
Hand drums called panderetas are central to its sound.
cultura.credit: Add verified photographer and image-source credit

cultura.name: La Salsa
cultura.origin: Caribbean, with important Puerto Rican contributions
cultura.description:
A lively dance-music style shaped by Caribbean and Latin American traditions.
Puerto Rican musicians and communities have played a major role in salsa’s development and worldwide popularity.
cultura.credit: Add verified photographer and image-source credit

cultura.name: Las Máscaras de Vejigante
cultura.origin: Especially associated with Loíza and Ponce
cultura.description:
Bright, expressive masks appear in traditional festivals and parades.
Their styles differ by locality and reflect layered African, Spanish, and Caribbean influences.
